From: L.G.Baumann
Email: 891270@beltel.co.za




I wrote to you in July 1998 (I
don't think my letter appeared
in Outlet) as follows:


"I recall reading in one of your
letters that a gold edge conn-
ector was more reliable so am
recording my experience for what
it is worth. I was always having
trouble at critical moments and
relied heavily on our local re-
pairman. I sensed that this also
caused other troubles to the
inside works.


When our repairer said he would
no longer be handling Spectrum
repairs I was very worried. How-
ever, he said that as a last job
he would fit a gold connector to
my Speccy (48K).

That was a full 6 years ago and
I have not had a problem of any
sort since. Perhaps I am just
lucky. I use a Speccy at home
quite a lot and have one switch
to turn on power to the Comput-
er, TV set, Plus D, small tape
recorder and Star NL-10 printer"

Well it seems that I now have to
face up to a problem in that I
have to replace the keyboard
membrane. Sometimes for example,
the keys for 1, 2, 3, 4 do not
connect.

Fortunately I bought 2 spares a
long time ago. I will have to do
the repairs myself.My purpose in
writing is to ask if any of your
readers can give me any hints on
procedure. Do I have to take any
special care when opening the
case? And are there any other
precautions that are necessary?

Any help that your readers can
give me would be greatly appre-
ciated.

May OUTLET coninue to thrive
throughout 1999.

                L.G. Baumann

Brian Cavers to L.G. Baumann

The earlier letter that you ref-
er to was in OUTLET 134 in Oct-
ober of last year.

Replacing a 48K key membrane is
fairly straightforward. The main
thing is to avoid kinking, bend-
ing sharply, or trapping the new
membrane.

Disconnect the power THEN any
add-ons such as +D, joystick,
etc. NEVER remove any add-ons
that plug in to the edge-conn-
ector at the back while the
Spectrum is powered up.

Turn the Spectrum upside down
and undo the screws.


Hold the two halves of the case
together and carefully turn it
back over the right way up.

Lift the top keyboard half up an
inch or so and peer under to see
what's what.

You should see two flat clear
celluloid type strips from the
top keyboard half down to the
bottom half.

Tilt the keyboard towards you to
get a clearer view and study how
and where the strips plug into
the circuit board in the lower
casing. Several thin metallic
stripes run down each of the
celluloid-like strips into the
sockets.


Note how these metallic stripes
line up with the metal connect-
ors in the socket and which side
of the celluloid they are on.

Grasp one of these celluloid
strips firmly between finger and
thumb as close as possible to
its socket.

Pull it up vertically firmly and
squarely to clear the socket. If
it doesn't come readily you can
wiggle it a bit but I suggest
you wiggle it in the same plane
as the WIDTH of the celluloid.

Push it back in and out a couple
of times so you get familiar
with the amount of pressure that
you need and how the stripes
line up with the connector.

Obviously, you don't really need
all this care with the bad memb-
rane since you presumably will
be throwing it away but it helps
to get the feel of inserting the
new one without any risk.

Remove the other connector in
the same way.

Turn the keyboard section over
and, if I remember correctly,
there is a covering film which
just pulls away and then the old
membrane is revealed. Note how
it lies. I think it rests over a
few plastic lugs. Just pull it
away.

Place the new membrane into the
same position and replace the
cover.

Holding everything in place,turn
over the keyboard.

Firmly grasp each celluloid
strip in turn and insert into
the appropriate sockets in the
same way you dealt with the old
ones.

Lay the keyboard slowly on top,
peering underneath to check that
no part of the celluloid strips
gets kinked or trapped.

Once resting on top, hold the
keyboard in position with your
fingers and insert the power
connector. Give a quick test to
see that all the main key areas
work(one or two keys at left and
right on each row is enough.


Pull out the power, turn over
the case - still holding the two
halves carefully together - and
screw it up again.

Cross your fingers.

Test again.

Go and have a cup of tea.

Other Spectrums are similar but
check for other connectors. The
+3 for example has a wire that
leads to an LED I think and it
also opens right to left like a
book. I think the 48K+ and 128K
might have a wire to the reset
button at the left if I remember
correctly.
                       Brian

From: Frank Bohan
Email: <franbo@globalnet.co.uk>




Dear Ron and Brian,

As the confusion about the Mill-
enium Bug continues,I would like
to point out that it is wrongly
named. It should be the...
Year-Before-The-Millenium Bug,
as the new millenium does not
really start until the year
2001. This is because there was
no Year Zero -the year 1AD foll-
owed 1BC.Therefore the thous-
andth year of the millenium is
Year 2000. Roman numerals did
not include a zero.


Apart from the fact that the
year 1AD was miscalculated, on
the 1st January 2000, it will be
Jewish year 5760. Chinese year
4697 will bring the year of the
dragon. In Islamic countries, it
will be 1421 and among Zoroastr-
ians, it will be year 2390.

In the incredibly complex Mayan
calendar the 1st January 2000
will be, if we reach it,...
12. 19. 06. 15. 01. 10 Imex (the
day of corn) 9 Kanklin(the month
of the dog of the underworld).

After all, it's only a number.

                   Frank Bohan

Brian Cavers to Frank Bohan







I think they should make NEXT
year 'zero' followed by 2000 the
year following that. Thereafter
everything should be 'normal'.
Otherwise EVERY thousand years
we're going to get this awkward
its-not-really-the-new-millenium
error. It's a bit like celebrat-
ing the New Year at one minute
to midnight. Why not sort it out
now and save ourselves all the
hassle every ten centuries? A
stitch in time saves nine.


The Italians should pay all the
costs. After all, it was their
fault. Pity they didn't miss out
the complete first century be-
cause I never liked calling the
1700's the '18th' century and
the 1900's the '20th' century.

I'm also curious whether 20th
Century Fox will change their
name next year. The name might
sound a bit old-fashioned in a
few years - a bit like 19th
'Century Fox' might have sounded
over the' last few decades.

                        Brian

From:Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER





Dear Brian,

          SURPLUS CD's

Another use for the "surplus" CD
disc ties in with Brian's quest-
ion on composition of colour.The
"pretty colours" reflected from
a CD can be used to examine the
spectrum of a light similar to
using a prism because the fine
data groves etched into the sil-
ver coating split up the light
by refraction.



Using this method I was able to
prove, for example,the text book
examples that sodium lamps are
single component yellow and mer-
cury lamps predominantly blue/
green. A tungsten lamp has far
more red component than a fluor-
escent tube but the latter has a
greater blue content. A yellow
gas flame as a result of poor
air mix is multiband spectrum
but a yellow flame produced by
burning salt is single spectrum
yellow.

Unfortunately the plastic coat-
ing is a pest and makes things
more difficult and it does take
a bit of practice to get decent
separation. A small light source
is better else colours tend to
merge back together.

           TV ANTICS


A while back, comment was passed
on the way some television prog-
rammes were presented. I had for
some time come to the conclusion
that the more the camera was
waved about, zoomed in and out
and seemed to be held by a
drunken cameraman or one being
chased round in circles by a
savage dog then the less inter-
esting the actual subject cover-
ed. There are exceptions where
an interesting subject is ruined
by producers with weird ideas.



Recently a series of programmes
about TV mentioned "camera tech-
nique" so the explanation is:

A still long shot just gives an
overall idea of a person's situ-
ation and surrounding whereas
the same person as a close up is
an exaggeration on real life.The
viewer sees such as exaggerated
eye movements that under normal
situations would not be noticed
so adding intensity and interest
in a situation that may not act-
ually be there.

A still camera gives a cooler
and detached view of what is
happening but moving cameras ab-
out a lot greatly increases the
perceived sense of pace and
gives added drama.

What was I saying -the more bor-
ing the subject, the greater the
camera-waving? You can watch a
programme or film with a lot of
camera movement and zooming but
if it is in keeping with the
"action" then it is not noticed.
However, when it's say, a chat
between two people, it is total-
ly ridiculous.


Likewise, lighting can be used
to effect to change the perceiv-
ed personality of a person from
a "good guy" with flat lighting
to a "villain " by harsh high-
lights and shadows to the face -
just like kids do with a torch!



I also get mad at the way that
after TV companies have spent
millions to transmit good quali-
ty pictures, the producers seem
to do everything they can to
mess them up with unnecessary
digitising, distorting, messing
up colours, superimposing unnec-
essary images, borders, multi-
picture screens, just to mention
a few. Just count how many times
that the picture is "messed
about" is, in fact, totally un-
necessary in the context of the
picture or subject itself.

When I want to check say, names
in the credits at the end of a
programme - what happens? They
are shoved into a minute box in
the corner - or the presenter is


superimposed and prances about
in front, waffling a load of
rubbish. If it's an American
programme then forget it because
the speed of scroll makes them
impossible to read and more seem
to be following suite. Cutting
out credits altogether seems to
be getting more common.

                 Malcolm Perry

From: Bernadette Dowsland, GOOLE

Dear Outlet,

Here's three gems of information
for all of you hardware fanatics
Firstly here's one idea that
definitely works on a +3...

Buy up any old PCW's at car boot
sales if they have two drives. I
suggest `10 maximum (I got one
last Sunday for a fiver and both
drives worked without trouble)

O.K. let's say you eventually
get two of these beasts. Drive
belts go on them just the same
as the +3's but if you've stuck
with your +3 for a number of
years you should be a dab hand
at changing them.

Now assuming you haven't defect-
ed to a PCW (Locoscript's horr-
ible - well, in my opinion) you
will now have two 3" 80 track
drives (two 40 track drives as
well you never know they might
come in handy)


Switch an 80 track drive in to
your +3 it will still read your
normal 40 track discs (a bit
slower). Rig up the spare 40
track drive as your B drive on
the +3. If you leave one PCW
intact then load CPM in the us-
ual way and with DISCKIT utility
format a batch of discs to 80
track format in drive 2 for use
in your +3 A drive.


You now have double the capacity
on your +3 A drive so transfer
your software using your 40
track B drive which will release
more 3" disks to be formatted
for your A drive. Yes I now have
such a system - I think I should
have presented Blue Peter.


Naturally you can still have a
3.5" B drive although you'll
have to be prepared to keep ch-
anging the edge connector plugs.


Sadly, Outlet in it's present +3
form would be confused and still
want you to swop sides of the
disk. [though just pressing a
key should skip over it - Ed]


Right the second handy tip...

+3 drive belts don't seem to
last long so try placing an old
worn out belt over another worn
out belt, it's feasable because
once again I've tried it and it
worked, proving two old belts
are better than one. Trust me
the flanges on the pulleys are
deep enough to keep two belts in
place.

The last tip has not been tested
but I feel certain it would work
here goes.

We all know how little software
has been written for the
Spectrum mouse either Kempston
or AMX, there is an historical
reason for this I guess....

The early Spectrums had no joy-
stick port; software houses only
write for hardware they know
your particular computer has as
standard (as a general rule).Now
Kempston joysticks did become so
common that the software houses
knew they'd have to cater for
them but alas not the mouse.
Mouse manufacturers wanted to
sell their interfaces to as many
Spectrum owners as possible so
once again plug it in the back
with the other bits and pieces.

Now the Amstrad CPC had a joy-
stick port from day one so AMX
designed thier rodent interface
to plug in there.They could have
brought out a later Spectrum
version to do the same but it
was too late.

Trojan did produce a +2/+3 light
pen to use the joystick socket,
a lightgun to use the keypad
socket and even the 48K lightpen
to use the tape input. This was
all very sensible and eased the
burden on the poor old expansion
bus BUT re-designing hardware if
you don't have to is a rarity.

O.K. obtain an Amstrad AMX mouse
if you can (yes I've got one).If
you're already using an Amstrad
monitor then you've got your 5v
jack plug with no messing.Remem-
ber you used to buy short leads
to convert Kempston joysticks to
ports 1 and 2 on the Amstrad
range of 128's? Well, you might
have to work out your own conv-
ersion lead but it should work
with trial and error.

The CPC AMX mouse interface hav-
ing its own power supply and not
having to plug into the Spectrum
expansion bus should not present
any danger of blowing up either
itself or your spectrum when
plugged into your joystick port.

The CPC AMX translates the mouse
motion into up/down/right/left
and fire etc so if you answer
Interface 2 or Spectrum port 1
or even re-define keys, the AMX
mouse should work in nearly all
your spectrum games, now isn't
that a prayer worth answering?

On this last tip I must once
again put a disclaimer: I think
it ought to work BUT please
don't send me your broken Spect-
rums, I'll BE OUT!  - Bernadette


From: Thomas Eberle



Dear Ron, dear Brian,

Thanks for printing my letter in
the last Outlet.

As a first response, Bernadette
Dowsland wrote in and ordered an
MB02. I remember her quite well,
after showing her the MB02 two
years ago at a show in Wetherby.
Bernadette also sent me a print
out of an article she wrote and
which will obviously be publish-
ed in Outlet.

To add a few comments to this
letter here are some words:-


First, thanks a lot for the ord-
er, Bernadette. In your article
you wrote much about the MB02
and the price. But the MB02 is
the "creme de la creme" for the
Spectrum. It is expensive and it
is only for users who are really
dedicated to the Spectrum. It
expands the possibilities but
only real users can take advant-
age of these possibilities. Oth-
ers might buy a +D and it's en-
ough for only playing games,etc.

But Sintech also has a lot of
other stuff: over 1300 titles of
software,mostly original releas-
es no re-releases by budget
software-houses. We've interest-
ing hardware: new Multiface 128,
SPEC-drum, ProfaceAT-Interface,
Melodik-AY-Soundinterface...

So anybody who want to know what
is new for the Spectrum, just
drop me a line.[see Sintech ad
in OUTVERTS - Ed].

I will also support OUTLET with
more articles about our prod-
ucts,so you will be well inform-
ed through OUTLET.

With Bernadette, there will be
at least four users of the MB02
in the UK!

Yours sinclairly,

              Thomas.

From: C. Bibby.

About Mr Zbruch, many thanks for
the hint, Ed.  [Eh? - Ed]

I have since written to Mr Higg-
inbottom of Orion about the
battery-operated five drive +3
in his possession. The reply
arrived instantly that same day
via Wells Fargo telegraph but I
couldn't decipher a word of it.
I have enquired at Smiths for a
relevent translator but they had
difficulty with the Alpha Beta
Gamma's of it also.

Then I had a brainwave. I de-
cided to check my ZX library
and, true to form, there wasn't
an Orion translator on the
Speccy either. Any hints?

On the subject of deciphering
fact from fiction, visitors from
elsewhere might have visited our
YTC stand at the NSSS last year.

       >>>>  WARNING  <<<<
This story has earned a "C" for
Caution.

    NOT FOR THE FRAIL MINDED

It's weird...

Eric and I arrived at the venue
early to beat the crowds.[that
IS weird - but, whatever turns
you on. - Ed] Mmm. It took an
hour or so to set out the YTC
stand. Three +3's, one of which
was battery-operated had soft-
ware loaded and running with
monitors and audios all perfect.

Satisfied all was well I went
for a wee. [Was that a big wee
or a wee wee? - Ed]

Imagine my horror returning to
the YTC stand to discover all of
the systems except the battery
operated +3 (booted with data
for the digitiser) had gone
down. Had I got my sums wrong?

Equipped for the unexpected, pat
kick and curse [who? - Ed] might
have had me overwhelmed
"digitally speaking" therefore
it seemed more sensible to first
check my power house.

Primary tests were followed by
secondary tests, no faults could
be identified in a hurry.


Then a glance at the main junc-
tion box revealed that the power
had been switched OFF while I
was away to leave only the batt-
ery operated +3 still digitis-
ing. Needless to say, nobody
owned up but nor did I detect
any giggles.

           VIRUS - BUG
     and now a true ZX style
   disembodied spirit, shadow,
            PHANTOM ?

   Moral:- BATTERY VOTED BEST
           FOR 2000

Cheerio

                   Colin

Brian Cavers to Colin Bibby

I didn't understand much of that
except for that bit where you
attacked some people and the bit
where you went for a wee, oh yes
and the bit where you got your
sums wrong.
                        Brian

From: Vic Bishop, LANCS



Dear Brian,

I am passing on a short tale
that I hope may be of some
interest to Spectrum fans and
indeed to all computer buffs. My
wife passed me the article (like
producing a rabbit out of a
Match box) which she brought
home from Church one recent
Sunday morning. It originated
from Fraser McGurk, a Trinity
member and goes as follows:-

You may be as fascinated as I am
by this story from Annie Blair
of Baltimore...


"Annie tells me that she read
that scientists busy on the US
space programme were checking
the position of the sun, moon
and planets 100 years from now,
to plan the flight of satell-
ites. They did it by using a
special computer to check over
past centuries; but to their
surprise, the computer suddenly
stopped -and a red light flashed
on - it had found a day missing.


You can imagine the consternat-
ion. Then one of the scientists
remembered a Bible story, where
the Lord was asked to make the
sun stand still for a whole day
-- you'll find it in Joshua,
Chapter 10.


They thought they'd solved the
problem, but no! for the compu-
ter was still 40 minutes short.
Could the Bible possibly have
the answer again? They checked -
and in Chapter 20 of second
Kings they found it, The sun was
commanded to go backwards for 10
degrees, as a sign.

You have to be a scientist to
know it (do you) but in that
sort of calculation 10 degrees
is exactly 40 minutes."

I found it an interesting story
- more probable I would think
than the set of calculations
being within the capabilities of
the Spectrum?. Not that I would
understand them anyway!


I found it a little ironic today
when, on attending a travel talk
about the Galapagos Islands the
speaker touched on the subject
of Darwin's theory and the fact
that it was rubbished by the
scientists of those days.

                 Vic Bishop

From: Ms B.Dowsland, GOOLE






Dear Outlet,

I read with interest Thomas
Eberle's letter in last month's
Outlet and I agree we are the
mother nation of the Spectrum
and should do more to further
its interests, BUT Thomas must
surely appreciate several of the
reasons for his up hill struggle
in this country, I'll elucidate
as a series of points he has in
selling the MB02 etc in this
country...


1. He translates his advert into
English BUT does not give an
approximate price in English
currency. To put it another way,
Deutsmarks have an uncanny knack
of making the price look bigger
than it really is, (about 2.8
times bigger just for the record
so there's a psychological barr-
ier to climb staight away with
those big Deutchmarke numbers)


2. It's not made in this country
so if anything goes wrong you
can't simply get in your car and
go and SORT IT OUT if letters
and phone calls bring no satis-
faction.


3. The language barrier,well you
know were a funny lot us British
we don't like learning other
peoples' languages - LET THEM
LEARN OURS!!

4. Maybe we're all planning to
upgrade to PC's, who cares? Bob
Brenchley will half kill me but
I think the MB02 looks more ex-
citing than a Sam.

5. The hassle of sending money
over there.

6. Maybe were all just tight _
whoops! I think I'm running out
of points here.

O.K. enough said!


Well I saw the MB02 last year at
a Wetherby show, so don't forget
Thomas has tried, he has demoed
the device in this country. So
today dawned bright and clear
and I got up said "What will I
do today, Oh! I know I'll go and
buy an MB02!"

Far fetched, well not really, I
trotted down to my local TSB and
asked them how much 290 DM was
in pounds (about `111) and how
was the best way to send it.They
said they would make me a cheque
in Deutschmarks but there was a
`12 surcharge(grabbing b*!*!??).
I thought about it and reasoned
if I was doing it - go for the
full monty i.e. the maximum SRAM
and the real time clock - after
all the surcharge is the same.

So with the surcharge the full
system (minus disk drives that
you can buy cheaply in this
country) is about `170 - not
cheap but there again how much
do I spend keeping an old banger
on the road in order to have a
job in the Summer. Anyway, the
money was "Only resting in my
account"

It won't have arrived by the
time most of you will be reading
this, BUT, if there's any MB02
owners in this country (and I
know there's at least one) feel
free to get in touch and togeth-
er we'll make the Spectrum
great!
                   Bernadette


Brian to Bernadette Dowsland

Well, the main thing is more
information. We have OUTVERTS
which is absolutely free to our
readers just begging to be used.

Readers will want to know what
the extra S-RAM Thomas mentioned
last month will actually do for
them and also about compatibil-
ity with +D, +3, etc.

Perhaps when you get it set up
you can do a review for us all,
Bernadette?

                       Brian.

Note how these metallic stripes line up with the metal connect- ors in the socket and which side of the celluloid they are on.

Grasp one of these celluloid strips firmly between finger and thumb as close as possible to its socket.

Pull it up vertically firmly and squarely to clear the socket. If it doesn't come readily you can wiggle it a bit but I suggest you wiggle it in the same plane as the WIDTH of the celluloid.

Push it back in and out a couple of times so you get familiar with the amount of pressure that you need and how the stripes line up with the connector.

Obviously, you don't really need all this care with the bad memb- rane since you presumably will be throwing it away but it helps to get the feel of inserting the new one without any risk.

Remove the other connector in the same way.

Turn the keyboard section over and, if I remember correctly, there is a covering film which just pulls away and then the old membrane is revealed. Note how it lies. I think it rests over a few plastic lugs. Just pull it away.

Place the new membrane into the same position and replace the cover.

Holding everything in place,turn over the keyboard.

Firmly grasp each celluloid strip in turn and insert into the appropriate sockets in the same way you dealt with the old ones.

Lay the keyboard slowly on top, peering underneath to check that no part of the celluloid strips gets kinked or trapped.

Once resting on top, hold the keyboard in position with your fingers and insert the power connector. Give a quick test to see that all the main key areas work(one or two keys at left and right on each row is enough.

Pull out the power, turn over the case - still holding the two halves carefully together - and screw it up again.

Cross your fingers.

Test again.

Go and have a cup of tea.

Other Spectrums are similar but check for other connectors. The +3 for example has a wire that leads to an LED I think and it also opens right to left like a book. I think the 48K+ and 128K might have a wire to the reset button at the left if I remember correctly. Brian

Предыдущее письмо, о котором вы упоминаете, было опубликовано в OUTLET 134 в октябре прошлого года.

Замена мембраны на 48K — дело довольно простое. Главное — не перегибать, не сгибать под острым углом и не защемлять новую мембрану.

Отключите питание, а ЗАТЕМ любые периферийные устройства, такие как +D, джойстик и т. д. НИКОГДА не извлекайте устройства, подключенные к краевому разъему сзади, пока Spectrum включен.

Переверните Spectrum вверх дном и выкрутите винты.

Придерживая обе половинки корпуса вместе, аккуратно переверните его обратно в нормальное положение.

Приподнимите верхнюю часть с клавиатурой примерно на дюйм и загляните внутрь, чтобы оценить обстановку.

Вы должны увидеть две плоские прозрачные полоски (напоминающие целлулоид), идущие от верхней половины с клавиатурой к нижней половине.

Наклоните клавиатуру к себе, чтобы лучше видеть, и изучите, как и куда эти шлейфы вставляются в разъемы на плате в нижней части корпуса. Вдоль каждого целлулоидного шлейфа к разъемам идут несколько тонких металлических дорожек.

Обратите внимание, как эти металлические дорожки совмещаются с металлическими контактами в разъеме и на какой стороне шлейфа они находятся.

Крепко возьмитесь за одну из этих целлулоидных полосок пальцами как можно ближе к ее разъему.

Потяните ее вертикально вверх, уверенно и ровно, чтобы вытащить из разъема. Если она не поддается сразу, можно слегка покачать ее, но я рекомендую покачивать только в плоскости ШИРИНЫ шлейфа.

Вставьте ее обратно и вытащите пару раз, чтобы привыкнуть к необходимому усилию и понять, как дорожки совмещаются с разъемом.

Очевидно, что со старой неисправной мембраной такая осторожность ни к чему, ведь вы ее, скорее всего, выбросите, но это поможет почувствовать процесс установки новой без всякого риска.

Таким же образом извлеките второй шлейф.

Переверните клавиатурную часть корпуса. Если я правильно помню, там есть защитная пленка, которая просто снимается, открывая старую мембрану. Запомните, как она лежит. Кажется, она держится на нескольких пластиковых штырьках. Просто снимите ее.

Уложите новую мембрану на то же место и верните подложку обратно.

Придерживая все на месте, переверните клавиатуру.

Крепко возьмите каждый шлейф по очереди и вставьте в соответствующие разъемы так же, как вы делали со старыми.

Медленно опустите клавиатуру сверху, заглядывая внутрь и проверяя, чтобы шлейфы нигде не перегибались и не защемлялись.

Когда она ляжет на место, придержите клавиатуру пальцами и вставьте разъем питания. Быстро проверьте работоспособность основных зон клавиатуры (достаточно проверить одну-две клавиши слева и справа в каждом ряду).

Выдерните питание, переверните корпус — все так же аккуратно придерживая обе половинки вместе — и снова закрутите винты.

Скрестите пальцы.

Проверьте еще раз.

Идите пить чай.

Другие модели Spectrum устроены аналогично, но обращайте внимание на дополнительные соединения. У +3, например, идет провод к светодиоду, и корпус раскрывается справа налево, как книга. У 48K+ и 128K, если мне не изменяет память, может быть провод к кнопке сброса (reset) слева.

### ТЕЛЕВИЗИОННЫЕ ВЫХОДКИ

Некоторое время назад уже обсуждалось то, как подаются некоторые телепередачи. Я уже давно пришел к выводу: чем сильнее мечется камера, чем больше зумов туда-сюда, и чем больше кажется, будто камеру держит пьяный оператор или человек, за которым по кругу гонится бешеная собака, тем менее интересна сама тема передачи. Бывают и исключения, когда интересную тему портят продюсеры со своими странными идеями.

Недавно в цикле передач о телевидении упомянули «операторскую технику», и вот как это объясняется:

Неподвижный общий план дает лишь общее представление о ситуации и окружении человека, тогда как крупный план того же человека гиперболизирует реальную жизнь. Зритель видит, например, подчеркнутые движения глаз, которые в обычной ситуации не были бы замечены, что придает напряженности и интереса ситуации, которой на самом деле может и не быть.

Неподвижная камера дает более спокойный и отстраненный взгляд на происходящее, а вот активное перемещение камер значительно усиливает ощущение динамики и добавляет драматизма.

О чем я и говорил: чем скучнее тема, тем сильнее машут камерой! Можно смотреть передачу или фильм с кучей движений камеры и наездов, но если это соответствует «действию», то этого не замечаешь. Однако когда речь идет, скажем, о простой беседе двух людей, это выглядит совершенно нелепо.

Точно так же можно эффективно использовать освещение, чтобы изменить восприятие человека: от «хорошего парня» при рассеянном свете до «злодея» с помощью резких бликов и теней на лице — прямо как дети балуются с фонариком!

Просто посчитайте, сколько раз картинку «уродуют» безо всякой необходимости для контекста самого изображения или сюжета.

Когда я хочу посмотреть, например, фамилии в титрах в конце передачи — что происходит? Их запихивают в крошечный квадратик в углу экрана — или поверх накладывают ведущего, который скачет на переднем плане и несет какую-то чушь.
